# Guardian Mesh

> Guardian Mesh is a guardian system for AI agents and software. Before an
> agent runs a command, calls a tool, or reaches the network, the action is
> evaluated by the Guardian Mesh daemon. Five enclaves examine it and the
> daemon returns a verdict (ALLOW, BLOCK, THROTTLE, ESCALATE) together with
> a signed, tamper-evident audit proof that anyone can re-check with
> VerifyProof — without trusting the daemon or AIMLDS.

Site: https://nrupala.github.io/guardian-mesh/
Source: https://github.com/nrupala/guardian-mesh
Descriptor (JSON): https://nrupala.github.io/guardian-mesh/guardian-mesh.json
Architecture (codetopo snapshot): https://nrupala.github.io/guardian-mesh/guardian-mesh-topology.json

## Components

- Sentinel — first check; runs the protocol firewall's 18 message checks
  over the sealed payload, context, and target.
- Gatekeeper — identity and permission; requires a live handshake session
  and a valid HMAC, otherwise the action is blocked.
- Witness — hashes the verdict and reason and signs the digest with
  ML-DSA-65 (post-quantum).
- Arbiter — applies policy and settles the final verdict; anything
  undecided defaults to BLOCK.
- Vault — seals the signed audit proof into a tamper-evident envelope
  (CRC32C integrity + ML-DSA-65 signature).
- Protocol Firewall — the 18 checks every message must pass.
- Handshake Bus — issues and tracks caller sessions.

## Interface

The daemon (Rust) serves gRPC service `GuardianMesh` with four calls:
Handshake (open a session and receive its HMAC key), Evaluate (judge a
sealed action before it runs), VerifyProof (re-check a signed audit
proof), Health. Callers open a handshake session, seal the action in an
HMAC-signed envelope, call Evaluate, obey the verdict, and keep the
proof. The same calls are available over gRPC-web.

A live deployment runs at https://guardian.aimlds.org — the working
control panel, connected to the daemon. Access is owner-only (Cloudflare
Access sign-in) while the deployment matures.

## Rules agents must respect

- BLOCK means do not proceed. THROTTLE means slow down. ESCALATE means
  stop and hand the decision to a human.
- An ALLOW covers one action exactly as sealed; any change needs a new
  evaluation.
- No answer from the daemon means BLOCK (fail closed), stated openly.
- Do not re-submit a blocked action unchanged, split it to evade checks,
  or route around the daemon.
- Verify proofs presented to you with VerifyProof before relying on them.

## Status — honest scope

Working today: the daemon, the five enclaves, the 18 firewall checks,
sealed envelopes, signed audit proofs, this website, the demonstration
control panel on this site (sample values; not connected to a daemon),
and the live control panel at guardian.aimlds.org connected to the
running daemon (owner-only sign-in).
Designed, not yet built: hardware (TEE) attestation, multi-node
consensus, public anchoring of proofs, and Lean 4 formal verification.

Guardian Mesh is built by AIMLDS. Its certificates vouch for the exact
item tested, against the policy named, on the date stamped — never for
someone else's deployment choices.
